JRSH's original response calls 0.34 the A+ giveback ceiling, while its retained
checklist requires at most 0.25 for A+ and allows 0.34 ordinarily. This is an
explanatory mismatch, not evidence that its published A-to-C lowering was wrong.
The prose, grade, source identity and receipt are preserved. JKHY is the real
unreviewed, Dollar-only A control; its red regime gate withholds entry.

`tools/continuity_check.mjs` assembles a two-row **presentation excerpt** from
this context. It is not a complete publication and cannot stand in for the
offline owning-function replay. It tests primary explanation, inspectable raw
commentary, comparison, saving, reload and deep links. Existing pipeline-generated
fixtures supply agreed, lowered and unavailable-reader controls. Neither the
retained excerpt nor those deterministic controls imply a new external read.

`node tools/page_smoke.mjs --only reader --shots <scratch>` exercises the same
retained excerpt in isolated browser contexts at 1280, 390 and 320 pixels in
both themes, including keyboard disclosure/focus, fit, unchanged raw text and
zero initial evidence requests. Screenshots are local renderer evidence, not
a journey through the live Pages publication.
